title: Intel Stock Rips Nearly 6% Overnight After Trump Confirms Apple Chip Manufacturing Deal
source_used: Stocktwits (date checked against Fox Business, 19 Jun 2026)
key_facts: Stocktwits: Intel shares jumped 5.7% in overnight trading after President Trump said in a Truth Social post that Apple had agreed to use Intel's foundry (contract chip-making) services; Apple shares gained 0.6%.
Trump wrote that Apple "has agreed to work with Intel to design and build its Chips in America"; he did not say which Apple chips Intel would make.
Trump said the US took a 10% stake in Intel (the government stake dates from last August) and claimed it was worth about $100 billion then and over $600 billion now.
Trump also said Nvidia agreed to build its first-level chips with Intel and that Elon Musk agreed to build a 'TerraFab' chip factory designed with Intel's technology team.
Bloomberg had reported the month before that Apple was considering Intel's and Samsung's US foundries for certain main processors; Intel supplied Mac processors from 2006 until about 2020.
Intel had just announced that its 18A-P manufacturing process had entered risk production (a low-volume trial stage); Intel's shares were up 228% for the year, per Stocktwits.

Date check: Stocktwits says the post came 'in the early hours on Thursday'; Fox Business (published 19 Jun 2026, 1:37am EDT, Reuters contributing) reported that Trump 'said Thursday', which is 18 Jun 2026.

Fox Business: Intel reportedly reached a preliminary agreement to make some chips for Apple after more than a year of talks, and Apple and Intel had not publicly detailed which chips or products would be involved.
quote_evidence: Intel Corp.’s stock jumped 5.7% in overnight trading ahead of Thursday after U.S. President Donald Trump said that Apple Inc. had agreed to use Intel’s foundry services.
Trump did not disclose which Apple chips Intel would manufacture.
President Donald Trump said Thursday that Apple has agreed to work with Intel on designing and producing chips in the U.S.
why_it_matters_hint: A big customer such as Apple would help Intel's contract chip-making business, but the claim rests on Trump's post and no chips are named.
notes: Older news re-dated: the Stocktwits page is listed as 5 Oct 2026, but its text (a Thursday Truth Social post, 'overnight trading ahead of Thursday') matches Fox Business's report of 19 Jun 2026 that Trump 'said Thursday', i.e. 18 Jun 2026. Other outlets covering the post (Taipei Times, TweakTown, Wccftech, Tech Times) are dated 18 to 20 Jun 2026. No new Apple-Intel facts found in today's window. Stocktwits cites Trump's post; neither company is quoted.
